title: Piston mass calculation
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the piston mass must be 10 kg.

title: Contact temperature calculation
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the ambient temperature must be 200 K.

title: Initial state identification
description: Important: The student must correctly identify the initial pressure as atmospheric and the initial volume using the given length and area.

title: Final pressure force balance
description: Important: The student must apply a force balance on the piston to derive the final gas pressure as p0 + mg/S.

title: Application of Boyle's Law
description: Important: The student must correctly apply Boyle's Law (p1V1 = p2V2) for the isothermal process to relate the initial and final states.

title: Isobaric process recognition
description: Important: For part (2), the student must recognize the process at constant pressure after the piston contacts the catches.

title: Application of Charles's Law
description: Important: The student must correctly apply Charles's Law (V/T constant) to find the final temperature from the known volumes and initial temperature.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student's work should demonstrate consistent use of SI units (e.g., converting cm² to m²).

title: Sign error in force balance
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly setting the final gas pressure as p0 - mg/S, reversing the direction of the weight force.

title: Volume misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Using an incorrect geometric length (e.g., 1.6 m for initial state or 1 m for final state) to calculate gas volumes.
